cards.explanation: The answer is to run with endurance the race set out for us. The writer says, "…let us run with endurance the race set out for us." (Hebrews 12:1) Notice the word endurance, friends. That's the kind of running he has in mind, and he says it with a great cloud of witnesses all around.

The answer is the sin that so easily entangles. The writer says to throw off "…every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles…" (Hebrews 12:1) Entangles is a great word. I have personally lost a fight with a mixer cord, so I know how a tangle goes.

The answer is Jesus. The writer says, "Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith…" (Hebrews 12:2) A runner who keeps looking around gets wobbly. Fix your eyes, friends, and keep them on Him.

The answer is for the joy set before Him. The writer says Jesus, "…for the joy set before Him endured the cross…" (Hebrews 12:2) Joy was set before Him, and He endured. After that, He sat down at the right hand of God's throne.
The answer is True. The writer says Jesus "…endured the cross, scorning its shame…" (Hebrews 12:2) The shame was real, and He scorned it. Then He sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

The answer is at the right hand of the throne of God. The writer says Jesus "…sat down at the right hand of the throne of God." (Hebrews 12:2) The cross came first. Then came the seat at God's right hand.

The answer is weary. We're told to consider Jesus "…so that you will not grow weary and lose heart." (Hebrews 12:3) You know weary: four snoozes in and the bed still wins. Looking at Jesus is the writer's cure.

The answer is False. The text says, "In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood." (Hebrews 12:4) Those readers had not gotten to that point. The coach is making a point, and the point is to keep going.
The answer is not lightly. The exhortation says, "My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord…" (Hebrews 12:5) Don't shrug it off, friends. It's worth listening to.

The answer is the one He loves. The exhortation says, "For the Lord disciplines the one He loves…" (Hebrews 12:6) It goes on to say, "…He chastises every son He receives." Discipline and love show up together in this verse.

The answer is father. The writer asks, "For what son is not disciplined by his father?" (Hebrews 12:7) Right before that, he says that God is treating you as sons. It's a father and son picture all the way through.

The answer is False. The writer says, "If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons." (Hebrews 12:8) So a child with no discipline isn't called a true son. Discipline is part of how God treats His sons.

The answer is to submit to Him much more and live. The writer asks, "Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?" (Hebrews 12:9) Much more, friends. We respected earthly fathers, and this is the Father of our spirits.

The answer is holiness. The writer says God disciplines us "…for our good, so that we may share in His holiness." (Hebrews 12:10) Earthly fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, and God does it for our good. If you left my idea of good up to me, it would be extra cookie dough, so I'm glad the aim here is holiness.

The answer is peace. The writer says discipline "…yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it." (Hebrews 12:11) Notice that it comes later on. It's a harvest, and harvests take time.

The answer is to strengthen them. The writer says, "Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees." (Hebrews 12:12) That Therefore points back to the verse before it. Discipline seems painful at the time, but later it yields "…a harvest of righteousness and peace…" to those who have been trained by it. So when the pain makes you feel limp and weak, the writer says to strengthen up and keep going, because the training pays off later.
The answer is True. The writer says, "Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed." (Hebrews 12:13) That's the exact line. The goal is healing.
